quick.summary: How to turn a finding into something your team can act on.
quick.takeaway: What changed, why it matters, what to try, how sure.

beats.line: I reported that checkout drop off went up. My manager said, so what?
A finding isn’t a next step yet. Add four things.
First, what changed, in one sentence.
Second, why it matters, in money or people.
Third, one thing to try, so there is a next step.
Fourth, how sure you are, so she knows how far to trust it.
You suggest. She decides. Suggestions make her faster.
Mobile drop off rose after the button moved. About two hundred lost orders a week.
Test moving it back? I’m fairly sure the button caused it.
Now she has something to say yes or no to.

quiz.question: Which addition turns a finding into a recommendation?
options: One thing to try next, and how sure you are
quiz.explanation: A recommendation gives the team a next step and how much to trust it.

quiz.question: At the associate level, it is best to report findings without suggesting anything.
quiz.explanation: You can still suggest one next step; your manager decides, but the suggestion speeds things up.
